_comment: Phase 225 plan 06 (CONN-03, MT5D-08). The cross-runtime oracle for the broker-server identity rule. Read by src/lib/venue-identity.test.ts (normaliseVenueServer, sameVenueServer, pickSameAccountHolder) and analytics-service/tests/test_venue_server_identity.py (normalise_venue_server, same_venue_server, pick_same_account_holder). HAND-TYPED: every expectation below was worked out by hand from the rule, never produced by either implementation, and every id and server is synthetic. The rule. NORMALISE: trim only space, tab, CR and LF from both ends (the SQL btrim(x, E' \t\r\n') of swap_account_slot and api_keys_venue_server_valid, so a vertical tab or a no-break space is NOT trimmed, in all three places), lower-case, blank becomes null, more than 128 characters after trimming becomes null, anything that is not a string becomes null. SAME: two servers are the same account when both are equal OR when EITHER is null (a key not yet backfilled matches on login alone). PICK: among the live keys of one login, tier 1 is a row whose server equals the new key's server (null equals null), tier 2 is a row where either side is null, tier 3 exists only in mode after_index_refusal (the old login-only index refused the write) and takes any row; the first non-empty tier wins and inside it the smallest id by plain string comparison, so the pick never depends on row order. ASCII letters only in the case-folded cases: JS toLowerCase, Python lower and SQL lower differ on a few non-ASCII code points. Do not add a case here without its expectation; both suites consume this file whole and assert every array is non-empty.

pick.name: fence: an exact server beats a null-server row
fence: a different-server row is not picked
after_index_refusal: the same rows pick the different-server row
fence: a null-server row is picked for any server
fence: a null new server picks a server-stamped row
fence: a null new server prefers a null-server row (null equals null) over a stamped one
empty rows pick nothing in fence mode
empty rows pick nothing after an index refusal
tier 1 tie: the smallest id wins, whatever the row order
tier 2 tie: two null-server rows, the smallest id wins
login-only tier tie: two different-server rows after a refusal, the smallest id wins
after_index_refusal still prefers an exact server over a different one
after_index_refusal still prefers a null-server row over a different one
a higher-tier row beats a smaller id in a lower tier
